'''Srinivasan Varadarajan''' (31 March 1928 – 11 May 2022) was an Indian [[chemist]], [[civil servant]], corporate executive and the former chairman of several [[Public sector undertakings in India|public sector undertakings]] such as [[Indian Petrochemicals Corporation Limited]] (IPCL), Petrofils Cooperative Limited, [[Engineers India Limited]] (EIL), and [[Bridge and Roof Company (India)]].<ref name="Indian Fellow">{{cite web | url=http://www.insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=N83-0861 | title=Indian Fellow | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=2 May 2016 | url-status=usurped | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160813061557/http://www.insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=N83-0861 | archive-date=13 August 2016 }}</ref>

== Education ==
Varadarajan hailed from [[Tamil Nadu]]. He obtained two master's degrees (MA and MSc) from [[Madras University]] and [[Andhra University]] and two doctoral degrees (Ph.D.) from [[University of Delhi]] and [[University of Cambridge]]. He worked as a faculty member at several educational institutions such as [[Delhi University]] (1949–53), [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (1956–57) and Department of Radiotherapeutics and University of Cambridge (1957–59).

== Awards ==
The Government of India awarded him the third highest civilian honour of the [[Padma Bhushan]] in 1985 for his contributions to society.<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web |date=2016 |title=Padma Awards |url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160204190707/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |archive-date=2016-02-04 |access-date=3 January 2016 |publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India}}</ref>

He was an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] (1983), [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (1972)<ref name="IAS Fellow">{{cite web |date=2016 |title=IAS Fellow |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Varadarajan,_Dr_Srinivasan |access-date=2 May 2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> and [[The World Academy of Sciences]] (1997).<ref name="TWAS Fellow">{{cite web |date=2016 |title=TWAS Fellow |url=http://twas.org/network/members/v |access-date=2 May 2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref>
